scenario_title: Severe hypercalcemia with suspected recurrent metastatic cancer

current_state.disposition: Admission to Hospital Medicine requested; monitored bed pending
current_state.code_status: Full code; goals-of-care discussion not yet completed

requesting_team.additional_context_contact: Jamie Example, spouse (synthetic), reachable through the bedside phone only
requesting_team.coverage_note: ED attending remains responsible until inpatient handoff. Prior oncology records are being requested from a fictional outside institution.

consult_request.urgency: Urgent; severe symptomatic hypercalcemia is being treated
consult_request.decision_needed: Advise the immediate malignancy workup and inpatient oncology plan for suspected recurrent metastatic lung adenocarcinoma with severe hypercalcemia and new lytic bone lesions.
consult_request.reason_now: The patient has confusion, corrected calcium of 14.8 mg/dL, acute kidney injury, and CT findings concerning for metastatic recurrence after a three-year lapse in oncology follow-up.
specific_questions: Which biopsy target and staging studies should be prioritized during this admission?
Should additional tumor-directed treatment be considered before tissue confirmation?
What oncology information is needed before discussing prognosis and treatment options with the patient and family?
consultant_action_requested: Review prior cancer history and current imaging
Recommend tissue diagnosis and staging sequence
Evaluate the patient after initial calcium stabilization
consult_request.accept_or_redirect_context: The patient is being admitted for medical stabilization. The ED is not asking Oncology to manage the acute hypercalcemia alone; it needs ownership of the malignancy-specific diagnostic plan.

chief_complaint: Progressive weakness, confusion, constipation, and right hip pain

symptoms.details: Previously independent in activities of daily living
Spouse reports slowed responses and two episodes of disorientation to date
No bowel movement despite over-the-counter polyethylene glycol
No fall; pain is worse at night
Approximately 8.2 kg by patient and spouse report

pertinent_negatives: No new focal weakness or sensory loss

conditions: Stage IIB right upper-lobe lung adenocarcinoma diagnosed in 2021
Right upper lobectomy followed by adjuvant platinum-based chemotherapy completed in 2022
Last oncology follow-up approximately 3 years ago
Former tobacco use; 32 pack-years, stopped in 2021

known_prior_cancer_data.original_pathology: Adenocarcinoma; detailed molecular report not available in current chart
known_prior_cancer_data.last_known_surveillance_scan: Reported as without recurrence in 2023; outside images unavailable

home_medications: Albuterol inhaler 2 puffs every 4 hours as needed
Acetaminophen 650 mg by mouth as needed for pain
Polyethylene glycol 17 g by mouth daily as needed

physical_exam.general: Tired appearing; dry mucous membranes; no acute respiratory distress
physical_exam.mental_status: Awake; oriented to person and place but states the date is three days earlier; follows two-step commands
physical_exam.cardiopulmonary: Mild tachycardia with regular rhythm; decreased breath sounds at right apex consistent with prior surgery
physical_exam.abdomen: Soft, mildly distended, no focal tenderness
physical_exam.musculoskeletal: Tender over right posterior pelvis; pain with right hip loading; no obvious deformity
physical_exam.neurologic: Strength 5/5 in all extremities; sensation intact; no clonus; gait not tested because of pain

electrocardiogram.interpretation: Shortened QT interval; no acute ischemic changes

findings: Postsurgical changes from right upper lobectomy
New 3.6 cm right hilar soft-tissue mass with narrowing of the right mainstem bronchus
Multiple new bilateral pulmonary nodules up to 1.1 cm
Multiple lytic lesions involving T11, L3, and the right iliac wing
No pathologic fracture identified on this study
ct_chest_abdomen_pelvis_with_contrast.impression: Findings are highly concerning for recurrent metastatic malignancy.

ct_head_without_contrast.findings: No acute hemorrhage, hydrocephalus, or large territorial infarct. Noncontrast CT does not exclude small metastases.

ed_treatment_and_actions.action: Normal saline intravenous infusion started after 1000 mL bolus
Zoledronic acid deferred pending repeat renal assessment and admitting-team decision
Repeat calcium and metabolic panel ordered for 20:00

pending_information.item: Repeat calcium, creatinine, magnesium, and phosphorus
Outside pathology, molecular testing, treatment summary, and surveillance imaging
MRI brain with and without contrast
pending_information.expected: Not yet ordered; decision requested from Oncology

ownership_and_next_steps.next_action: Oncology review of imaging and recommendation for biopsy target and staging sequence
ownership_and_next_steps.escalation_trigger: Notify ED attending immediately for worsening mental status, new focal neurologic deficit, arrhythmia, hemodynamic instability, or inability to maintain hydration

intended_workflow_challenges: The acute metabolic problem and the malignancy-specific question have different owners
Important outside cancer records are missing
The participant must distinguish suspected recurrence from confirmed pathology
The note and board should preserve the biopsy, staging, and follow-up plan
high_signal_facts: Symptomatic severe hypercalcemia with suppressed parathyroid hormone
Prior lung adenocarcinoma and a long gap in oncology follow-up
New hilar mass, pulmonary nodules, adrenal nodule, and lytic bone lesions
Acute kidney injury affects immediate treatment choices
No focal neurologic deficits or pathologic fracture identified
intentional_uncertainties: Recurrence is strongly suspected but not tissue-confirmed
The safest and highest-yield biopsy target has not been selected
Brain staging has not been completed
